claim: LangChain's Deep Agents framework defines five distinct context types that require separate management -- input context, runtime context, context compression, context isolation, and long-term memory -- each with different scope (static per run, per-run propagating to subagents, automatic on threshold, per-subagent, persistent across threads).
stance_target: a rigorous software-factory architecture must separately address multiple distinct categories of agent context, not treat 'context management' as a single monolithic concern
quoted_support: Deep agents include built-in mechanisms for managing context across long-running sessions. This page provides an overview of the different kinds of context your deep agent has access to and manages.

claim: Built-in content offloading in Deep Agents activates when tool call inputs or results exceed a 20,000-token threshold: large file writes/reads are replaced in conversation history with a filesystem pointer, and large tool results are substituted with a file path reference plus a 10-line preview.
stance_target: concrete, specific token thresholds for automated context compression infrastructure
scope_conditions: LangChain Deep Agents default configuration, deepagents>=0.6.6
quoted_support: Content offloading happens when tool call inputs or results exceed a token threshold (default 20,000) ... the deep agent offloads the response to the configured backend and substitutes it with a file path reference and a preview of the first 10 lines.

claim: Automatic summarization in Deep Agents triggers at 85% of the model's max_input_tokens, keeps 10% of tokens as recent context, and falls back to a fixed 170,000-token / 6-message trigger if no model profile is available; it produces both an in-context structured summary (intent, artifacts, next steps) and a full-text filesystem record for later retrieval.
stance_target: precise configuration parameters for automated agent memory compression relevant to continuous operation pillar
scope_conditions: LangChain Deep Agents SummarizationMiddleware default behavior
quoted_support: Triggers at 85% of the model's max_input_tokens from its model profile. Keeps 10% of tokens as recent context. Falls back to 170,000-token trigger / 6 messages kept if model profile is unavailable.

claim: Subagents in Deep Agents solve the context-bloat problem by running with their own fresh context and returning only a single final report to the main agent, which keeps the main agent's context window clean even when the subagent performs many tool calls internally.
stance_target: context isolation via a Director/Worker subagent architecture as the mechanism for controlling blast radius of context pollution
quoted_support: Subagents isolate this work—the main agent receives only the final result, not the dozens of tool calls that produced it... Subagent runs with its own fresh context, Subagent executes autonomously until completion, Subagent returns a single final report to the main agent, Main agent's context stays clean.

claim: Skills use progressive disclosure -- only skill frontmatter is loaded into the agent's context at startup, with full skill content loaded only when the agent determines it is relevant to the current task -- explicitly contrasted with memory files (AGENTS.md) which are always loaded regardless of relevance.
stance_target: SOP-to-Agent-Skill pillar: skill-loading architecture (progressive disclosure) is a distinct design pattern from always-on memory injection
quoted_support: The agent reads frontmatter from each SKILL.md at startup, then loads full skill content only when it determines the skill is relevant. This reduces token usage while still providing specialized workflows... Unlike skills, memory is always injected—there is no progressive disclosure.

claim: Explicit best practice for subagent design is instructing subagents to return concise summaries (example given: under 500 words) rather than raw search results or detailed tool outputs, to prevent context bloat from propagating up to the main orchestrating agent.
stance_target: concrete prompt-engineering pattern for Director/Worker agent architectures
quoted_support: Keep subagent responses concise: Instruct subagents to return summaries, not raw data: ... IMPORTANT: Return only the essential summary (under 500 words). Do NOT include raw search results or detailed tool outputs.
